response.markdown_report:
## Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Endpoint and interior targets receive different context; weighting can test inference alignment. Endpoint masking already exists in BERT4Rec [1]. (2) Per-example normalization changes sequence influence. With equal group sizes, equal group weighting exactly equals averaging concatenated example losses; it is not an additional mechanism. (3) Qualitative feedback motivates investigating recent relevance, but neither feedback nor sampled margins demonstrates a training defect.

**Related work.** (1) BERT4Rec describes endpoint masking, but released generators differ; inspect the supplied baseline rather than assume its mixture [1]. (2) Recency sampling motivates temporal task allocation, while changing prefix draws also changes target age and context length [2]. (3) Sampled rankings and convergence can alter comparisons [3,4]. Preserve benchmark selection and report realized compute and supervision.

## Framework and directions

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed investigation |
|---|---|---|
| Objective alignment | Random and endpoint masking [1] | Weight-only ablation |
| Temporal relevance | Recency sampling [2] | Matched recent/older context ablation |
| Evaluation validity | Sampled ranking; convergence [3,4] | Paired benchmark outcomes and compute accounting |

## Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

1. **Controlled supervision weighting: 3/6/3.** Originality: + explicit allocation control; − established mechanisms and possible algebraic equivalence. Potential: + interpretable experiment; − gains uncertain. Difficulty: + small loss change; − exact baseline matching needs care.
2. **Recency-biased prefix endpoints: 4/6/4.** Originality: + combines temporal sampling and endpoint tasks [2]; − familiar principle. Potential: + addresses recent relevance; − may suppress persistent interests. Difficulty: + sampler modification; − target-age/context-length controls required.
3. **Matched-context diagnostic: 3/6/3.** Originality: + controlled context comparison; − standard perturbation method. Potential: + measures right-context benefit; − no direct ranking improvement. Difficulty: + reuses scoring; − matching requires care.

## Selected experiment: balanced supervision

At 10% progress, retain idea 1 but isolate weighting. Preserve the corrected baseline’s exact loss as control. Freeze architecture, optimizer, prefix draws, corruption masks, truncation and reduction; compare its effective group weights against α=0.5. If identical, skip the duplicate experiment. Treat per-example normalization as a separate ablation, not part of the weight-only claim.

Use nonempty endpoint-only and ordinary reconstruction groups; hide every supervised target with reserved MASK. Specify fixed-count masking, target eligibility, replacement and zero-target policies from the baseline. Endpoint inputs retain clean preceding context. Combine both losses before one optimizer step. Record group sizes, terminal-target frequency, masks/example, context lengths, updates, epochs and GPU-seconds.

Preserve four categories, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, 200-epoch/200-update caps, appended-mask inference, final-nonpadding readout, checkpoint consistency and diagnostic interfaces. Compare under equal GPU-time allocations within 43,200 GPU-seconds, charging diagnostics and failures.

Predeclare comparisons and disclose validation queries [5]. Select by pinned macro HR@10; retain paired user hits and within-category bootstrap macro differences. Intervals exclude seed variability and adaptive-selection bias. Full-catalog diagnostics remain auxiliary. Popularity shortcuts and validation overfitting remain possible. No gains are measured.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643; [3] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/; [4] https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483; [5] https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html

idea.description: Test α=0.5 endpoint-versus-reconstruction weighting against the corrected baseline’s exact objective, changing only group weights in each category’s single BERT4Rec model. Keep per-example normalization as a separately identified ablation.
idea.motivation: Appended-mask inference lacks right context, whereas interior reconstruction can use it. Controlling supervision allocation tests whether emphasizing inference-like tasks improves validation ranking. Equal weighting is algebraically redundant when the baseline already averages equally sized groups of scalar example losses; establish objective equivalence before spending training budget.
idea.implementation_notes: Use the supplied corrected baseline without assuming that its sampling or loss matches either the paper or released reference code. Preserve an explicit baseline control and document its exact reduction, endpoint frequency, masking policy and optimizer-step construction. Predeclare the baseline and one weight-only candidate, omitting the candidate if its objective is identical. For both arms, use identical seeded user/prefix draws, truncation, group membership and corruption masks. Preserve the baseline's within-group reduction: token means remain token means; example means remain example means. If the baseline globally averages token losses, reproduce it exactly as sum_g(S_g)/sum_g(N_g), equivalently weighting group token means by N_g/sum_g(N_g); the candidate uses 0.5 times each group token mean. If baseline reduction is over examples, use example counts instead. Never silently replace another baseline loss with catalog cross-entropy. Record the actual formula when the supplied baseline becomes available. The original proposed per-example normalization means averaging supervised losses within examples and then within groups; evaluate it only as a separate, explicitly labeled normalization change if budget permits. With equal example counts, its equal group weighting equals a concatenated example mean. Endpoint examples must contain a training-prefix target replaced by MASK, with clean preceding history and truncation reserving its position. Ordinary reconstruction must preserve the baseline's eligible positions, mask-count rule, replacement rule and nonempty-target policy; every supervised input position must be MASK under this task's contract. Do not introduce endpoint fallback for empty masks. If these required groups or masking rules differ from the corrected baseline, retain the exact baseline arm and add a matched-construction control before attributing improvements to weights alone; reduce the comparison set if necessary to respect compute. Keep architecture, optimizer and total batch size fixed, and combine group losses before one backward pass. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, four-category routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Use equal predeclared GPU-time allocations under the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget, including validation, diagnosis and failed trials. Report hardware, completed updates/epochs, supervised targets per update and total targets, group sizes, terminal-target frequency, masks per example and retained context length. Keep one independently trained checkpoint per category, matching embedded predictor architecture, appended-mask inference and final-nonpadding readout. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) and every ModelView interface. Measure only valid supervised MASK positions; unavailable quantities remain null. Group-specific losses and margins are auxiliary measurements, not established predictors of HR@10. Do not infer compatibility, ownership, ratings or latent traits from unavailable data. Select exclusively with the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. If host outputs expose paired user hits, report candidate-only and baseline-only counts, dataset delta=(candidate-only−baseline-only)/200, and paired bootstrap intervals by resampling users within each category and equally averaging category deltas. One net hit changes category HR@10 by 0.5 percentage points. These intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidates; they exclude seed variation and adaptive search bias. Disclose every validation query, freeze the final choice before held-out evaluation, and treat reused-validation gains as exploratory. Supporting full-catalog diagnostics must use only permitted validation targets and count against budget. Check frequency/history-length breakdowns for possible popularity shortcuts without changing the selection metric. No improvement has been observed or established.
idea.pseudocode:
baseline_spec = document_supplied_corrected_baseline()
comparison_set = predeclare_exact_baseline_and_weight_only_candidate()
# If group construction must change, include a matched-construction control.
# If alpha=0.5 is algebraically identical to the control, omit that duplicate.
for arm in comparison_set:
    for category in four_categories:
        initialize_one_corrected_bert4rec(seed=42)
        reset_identical_seeded_training_streams()
        for epoch in range(max_epochs_at_most_200):
            for step in range(200):
                if predeclared_gpu_time_allocation_exhausted():
                    stop_training()
                groups = draw_identical_prefixes_and_masks_for_this_update()
                assert_all_supervised_inputs_are_reserved_MASK(groups)
                assert_endpoint_group_has_clean_preceding_context(groups)
                losses = compute_baseline_supervised_loss_terms(model, groups)
                if arm == 'exact_baseline':
                    loss = baseline_spec.exact_reduce(losses)
                elif arm == 'matched_construction_control':
                    loss = baseline_spec.exact_reduce(losses)
                else:
                    endpoint_mean = preserve_baseline_within_group_reduction(losses.endpoint)
                    reconstruction_mean = preserve_baseline_within_group_reduction(losses.reconstruction)
                    loss = 0.5 * endpoint_mean + 0.5 * reconstruction_mean
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                record_realized_supervision_and_compute()
        save_one_category_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor()
# A separate normalization ablation, if predeclared and budgeted:
# group_mean = mean_over_examples(mean_over_supervised_targets(losses))
# For equal group sizes, 0.5*mean(A)+0.5*mean(B) == mean(concat(A,B)).
# Inference: left-pad retained history plus appended MASK;
# read the final nonpadding position and score with that category's one model.
# Compare arms using host macro validation HR@10 and paired hit diagnostics;
# freeze the chosen configuration before held-out evaluation.

originality.positive: Explicit objective accounting separates supervision weighting from normalization and sampling, producing a useful controlled experiment.
originality.negative: Both masking modes are established, and equal weighting can be algebraically identical to an existing balanced-batch objective.

future_potential.positive: A clean comparison can establish whether supervision allocation deserves further study before adding architectural complexity.
future_potential.negative: The weighting is heuristic, the benchmark has limited validation resolution, and better alignment need not improve ranking or immediate usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The candidate primarily changes loss coefficients and retains the same inference architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducing exact baseline reduction, controlling random streams and accounting for supervision and compute require more care than a simple loss edit.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item reconstruction and appended-mask next-item prediction.
Describes last-item-only training examples to address inference alignment.
limitations: Does not establish a 50:50 mixture or its benefit on this benchmark.
Paper descriptions and released generator paths differ; the corrected supplied baseline must be inspected by the implementing host.
Interior reconstruction can use right context unavailable at appended-mask inference.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec reference data generator
contributions: Exposes concrete target-selection, replacement and force_last behavior.
Provides implementation details needed to distinguish mask-count selection from mask-token replacement.
limitations: Its default generator path should not be assumed to implement every training mechanism described in the paper.
Its behavior is not evidence of the supplied corrected baseline's exact behavior.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec reference training loss
contributions: Implements a weighted average over valid flattened masked targets.
Clarifies why global token averaging can differ from averaging per-sequence means.
limitations: Does not validate changing normalization or group weights on the prescribed datasets.
Source behavior must not be substituted for the host baseline without an explicit control.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Motivates controlling the temporal distribution of sequential recommendation training tasks.
limitations: Does not directly validate endpoint-versus-reconstruction weighting here.
Recency-biased prefixes can jointly change target age and retained context length.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics and reverse model comparisons.
limitations: Does not identify an optimal BERT4Rec objective.
Does not authorize changing the pinned benchmark selection criterion.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec replicability study
contributions: Highlights the influence of implementation details and convergence time on BERT4Rec comparisons.
limitations: Does not establish a benefit from the proposed weighting.
Equal compute allocations can still produce different supervision counts and convergence states.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how optimizing a finite validation criterion can cause selection bias.
limitations: Ordinary paired confidence intervals do not correct adaptive validation reuse.
The fixed single-seed task cannot estimate training-seed variability.

related_work.title: NIST: McNemar Test
contributions: Describes paired binary-outcome testing using discordant pairs.
limitations: Does not remove adaptive selection bias or directly supply a four-category macro confidence interval.
